B_access_pricing.mcp_access_cost_details: No separate fee for the MCP connection is stated in the reviewed official sources. A Ramp account and access to the chosen AI client are required; ChatGPT setup requires Plus or Pro.
B_access_pricing.linked_software_cost: Ramp Free is listed at $0 per user per month. Ramp Plus is paid and billed per user; the reviewed official pricing material did not state its price. Enterprise is contact sales.
B_access_pricing.pricing_model_details: Ramp Plus billing is per eligible active user. Ramp Free is available. Bill Pay may have transaction fees; these are charges for the linked Ramp software, not a stated MCP fee.
B_access_pricing.other_access_restrictions: Company admins can allow all, no, or selected employees to connect. Role-level controls require Ramp Plus. Tools and data depend on the connected user’s permissions, role, admin controls, scopes, client and environment. Custom-client redirect URIs must be allowlisted. ChatGPT setup requires Plus or Pro.
B_access_pricing.restrictions_controlled_by: Ramp vendor and organization admins; the user authorizes their own connection. The AI-client vendor controls its own subscription requirements.

Provided metadata identifies Ramp as the authorization server and advertises bearer tokens in the Authorization header. DCR is advertised at https://mcp.ramp.com/register. D_server_side_logic.additional_logic: 1. The canonical hosted reference lists read and write operations but publishes no MCP annotations (readOnlyHint, destructiveHint, idempotentHint, openWorldHint). Tool types are listed in actions.json from descriptions and names. 2. User-confirmation patterns appear in tool descriptions and parameters, including preview/confirm flows and required confirmation fields; hosted handler enforcement is not independently inspectable. Product approval workflows apply to transactions, reimbursements and unified requests. 3. OAuth scopes are broad and include read and write scopes. Ramp says the connection inherits the signed-in user’s role and permissions. Admins can set company access, and Ramp Plus adds role-level controls. Custom client redirect URIs require exact allowlisting. Token lifetime is NOT FOUND; revocation endpoint is advertised. 4. Production and sample-data endpoints are documented. Runtime tool access varies by scopes, identity, controls, client and environment. No URL/header tool filters or read-only mode for this endpoint were found. 5. Data access is bounded by the connected user’s Ramp permissions and business context. No general hosted MCP PII masking policy was found. Some tools expose agent card credentials; do not infer that all card secrets are hidden. 6. Support docs say a query over 100 rows returns no rows and should be narrowed; reporting tools separately describe paginated results and some 1,000-row caps. ETL operation capacity errors are documented. Hosted rate limits and per-call prices are NOT FOUND. 7. Tool schemas publish typed parameters and many descriptions require exact IDs or values. Tool descriptions document corrections/constraints, including that one-time funds use permanent increases even if temporary is supplied. Hosted operator-side argument rewriting and unknown-argument handling are NOT FOUND. 8. Ramp says calls are attributed to the signed-in user; admins can review connected-tool identity, status and last use. Audit log tools and audit-log scopes exist. MCP-specific telemetry collection and opt-out are NOT FOUND. 9. The official list includes ramp_submit_agent_nps. Ramp support also suggests asking an AI tool to submit feedback. Runlayer lists submit_feedback, which is not in the canonical names. 10. Agent guidance is embedded in tool descriptions; ramp_reporting_get_skill returns a reporting workflow skill. Ramp separately publishes CLI guidance and skills. Instructions in descriptions are recommendations to the model unless the server’s tool schema/operation enforces them. 11. Hosted cross-call memory or persistent agent personalization is NOT FOUND. The older local server has an ephemeral in-memory SQLite ETL database. 12. The hosted reference is a large shared catalog whose runtime tools depend on identity, scopes, client and environment; this is dynamically variable availability. The old local stdio server is a different architecture and is not the deployed endpoint. 13. No general arbitrary API-request or run-script tool was identified. The catalog contains constrained query tools: ramp_execute_analyst_query is described as read-only SQL with catalog/domain requirements; ramp_reporting_query uses a semantic dataset contract. The legacy local server’s execute_query accepts SQL against its in-memory tables, but that code is not the hosted endpoint.

D_server_side_logic.server_structure_explanation: The canonical list is shared across MCP and CLI, while the available tools vary by authenticated identity, scopes, admin controls, client and environment. This creates runtime-dependent tool availability. The hosted server’s internal hierarchy or sub-server architecture is NOT FOUND.

E_aggregated.action_count_comment: The official tool reference exists at https://agents.ramp.com/docs/reference/agent-tools. It states 224 tools; parsing the captured reference found 226 distinct official names. Added 24 catalogue-only names: 22 from Composio’s Ramp MCP toolkit (version 20261018_00; one overlaps Runlayer), plus ramp_token_info and submit_feedback from Runlayer. Catalogue counts: Runlayer 124, Composio 213, mcp.directory 16, Claude connector directory 16 (different endpoint), Gamut lists an older local-server tool set, and Tedix reports zero verified tools. Catalogue-only actions are appended after official actions. Third-party names from the Claude listing and older/different endpoint catalogues were excluded from this endpoint’s action list.

E_aggregated.token_method: Approximate characters divided by four from a JSON serialization of the 226 official reference entries’ names, descriptions and parsed parameter schemas; no hosted initialize instructions or annotations were available. Catalogue-only names excluded.
E_aggregated.human_can_agent_cannot: The support article says chat attachments are not automatically passed to MCP, so a user cannot simply attach a receipt image/PDF and have it forwarded as an MCP input; the current tool reference separately lists receipt upload-link and receipt-file tools, so supported upload paths depend on client and workflow. The support article says bill approvals are unavailable through the AI connection, while the current official tool reference lists ramp_approve_or_reject_bill; availability is therefore unresolved. The complete set of manual-only Ramp product operations was not established.

F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: Tool descriptions instruct agents to obtain explicit user confirmation for selected operations and to follow particular search, reporting and workflow sequences. Ramp recommends the CLI for coding agents. These model-facing instructions are not evidence of server enforcement unless enforced by parameters or the operation itself. Verbatim examples appear in D.
F_documentation.governance_promises: Ramp says the connection inherits the signed-in user’s role and permissions and attributes calls to that user. Admins can control which employees connect; Ramp Plus adds role-level controls. The privacy policy says personal-data retention depends on category, product, purpose and legal requirements; customer-directed AI functionality is governed by the applicable agreement and DPA. The integration page says Ramp may share data with subprocessors and other third parties as described in its platform agreement. MCP-specific model-training, prompt retention and masking terms were not found.
F_documentation.promises_to_user: "Your Ramp permissions come with you." Ramp describes secure connection and user-attributed actions, and provides production and sample-data connection options.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: Permission inheritance and action attribution are documented product claims; the hosted server code is closed, so handler-level enforcement could not be checked. OAuth metadata objectively establishes the authorization server, grants, PKCE, registration and scopes. Tool descriptions contain additional behavioral guidance, some with confirmation parameters; the docs do not establish enforcement for every instruction. MCP-specific retention or AI-training promises were not found.

contradictions: The official tool reference says its snapshot includes 224 tools, but the captured page contains 226 distinct tool-name headings.
The support article says bill approvals are not available through the AI connection, while the current official tool reference lists ramp_approve_or_reject_bill.

The support article says Ramp MCP does not expose receipt upload as an MCP tool, while the current official reference lists ramp_request_receipt_upload_link and ramp_upload_receipt_file. The same support article says chat file attachments are not automatically forwarded.

The official OAuth metadata advertises many write scopes, including cards, bills, reimbursements and transactions, while support documentation describes selected operations as unavailable; the current tool reference includes at least some of those operations.

Claude’s connector directory lists a read-only Ramp connector at https://ramp-mcp-remote.ramp.com/mcp with 16 tools, including submit_feedback. That is a different host/endpoint from the input endpoint and its tools were not used as input-endpoint actions.

Third-party catalogues report different inventories: Runlayer 124, Composio 213, and mcp.directory 16. Runlayer and Composio contain names absent from the canonical reference; only those catalogue-only names are marked third-party in actions.json.

The public ramp-public/ramp_mcp code is a local stdio implementation using client credentials and a demo-by-default environment; the input endpoint is hosted and uses browser OAuth. The public code is not the deployed server.
observations_for_research: Ramp publishes a shared MCP/CLI tool reference while documenting runtime variation by user identity, scopes, admin controls, connected client and environment.
The hosted OAuth metadata exposes read and write scopes across financial domains, while actual available tools are described as permission-dependent.
Agent-facing behavior guidance appears extensively inside tool descriptions, alongside some explicit confirmation parameters and preview-confirm flows.
Ramp exposes separate production and sample-data endpoints and recommends a distinct CLI for coding-agent workflows.
The current official tool reference and support article appear to reflect different tool generations for bill approvals and receipt uploads.
notes: Checked links.json, pages/ and both local repositories. The official reference page was parsed for tool headings and schemas; its stated total differs from extracted names. The older ramp_mcp repository was read but is not the hosted server; its relevant tool registration, handlers, API client, pagination, instructions and ephemeral SQLite logic were inspected. The official legal URLs were checked; the privacy policy was also reviewed through Ramp’s official search-indexed page. Official privacy policy was updated 2026-10-13. Catalogue warnings or endpoint mismatches were not used to replace the official tool list. Catalogue-only parameters were unavailable and are marked NOT PUBLISHED.
